title: Which country has the best schools?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: a service economy based on highly skilled industries such as IT, finance or advanced engineering
without considering, or being influenced by

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I’m Phil. And I’m Beth. So, Beth, we're talking about the best education systems in the world today.
sentences.zh: 我是Phil。我是Beth。Beth，今天我们来聊聊世界上最好的教育体系。

sentences.en: You went to school here in Britain. What do you think of the British education system?
sentences.zh: 你是在英国上的学。你觉得英国的教育体系怎么样？

sentences.en: Do you think it could be the best? I think that it's quite good, there's probably a couple of things that I personally would change about it, but I would say it's quite good, but maybe not the best in the world.
sentences.zh: 你觉得它算不算是最好的？我觉得它挺不错的，可能我个人会有那么一两点想要改变，但我觉得它相当不错，不过也许不是世界上最好的。

sentences.en: Well, in this programme, we're going to be talking about the Pisa rankings.
sentences.zh: 在这期节目中，我们将讨论Pisa排名。

sentences.en: The rankings are based on tests carried out by the OECD, that's an international organisation, every three years.
sentences.zh: 这些排名基于OECD（一个国际组织）每三年开展一次的测试。

sentences.en: The tests attempt to show which countries are the most effective at teaching maths, science and reading.
sentences.zh: 这些测试试图展示哪些国家在教授数学、科学和阅读方面最有效。

sentences.en: But is that really possible to measure? Well, here is former BBC education correspondent Sean Coughlan talking to BBC World Service programme 'The Global Story'.
sentences.zh: 但这真的能衡量吗？这里是前BBC教育记者Sean Coughlan在接受BBC世界服务部节目《The Global Story》采访时的谈话。

sentences.en: When they were introduced first of all, that was a very contentious idea, because people said 'how can you possibly compare big countries… how can you compare America to Luxembourg or to, you know, or to parts of China, or whatever?'
sentences.zh: 当这些测试最初推出时，这是一个极具争议的想法，因为人们说“你怎么可能比较大国……你怎么能把美国和卢森堡相比，或者和，你知道的，或者和中国的一部分相比，诸如此类？”

sentences.en: Sean said that the tests were contentious.
sentences.zh: Sean说这些测试极具争议。

sentences.en: If something is contentious, then it is something that people might argue about – it's controversial.
sentences.zh: 如果某事是 contentious 的，那么它就是人们可能会争论的事情——也就是有争议的。

sentences.en: So, at first, Pisa tests were contentious because not everyone believed it was fair to compare very different countries.
sentences.zh: 所以，起初Pisa测试备受争议，因为并非所有人都认为比较截然不同的国家是公平的。

sentences.en: Phil, I've got a question for you about them.
sentences.zh: Phil，我有一个关于它们的问题要问你。

sentences.en: So, in 2022, Singapore was top of the reading rankings.
sentences.zh: 在2022年，新加坡的阅读排名高居榜首。

sentences.en: But which of these countries came second?
sentences.zh: 但以下哪个国家排名第二？

sentences.en: Was it: a) The USA? b) Ireland? or, c) The UK?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 美国？b) 爱尔兰？还是 c) 英国？

sentences.en: I think it might be b) Ireland. OK. Well, we will find out if that's correct at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可能是 b) 爱尔兰。好的。嗯，我们将在节目结束时揭晓答案是否正确。

sentences.en: A common pattern in the Pisa rankings is that the most successful countries tend to be smaller.
sentences.zh: Pisa排名中一个普遍的规律是，最成功的国家往往体量较小。

sentences.en: Talking to BBC World Service programme 'The Global Story', Sean Coughlan tells us that many large countries from Western Europe don't score that highly in the rankings.
sentences.zh: Sean Coughlan在接受BBC世界服务部节目《The Global Story》采访时告诉我们，许多西欧的大国在排名中得分并不那么高。

sentences.en: They're being outpaced and outperformed by these fast, upcoming countries – you know, Singapore, or Estonia, or Taiwan, or those sort of places which we don't historically think of as being economic rivals, but I suppose the argument for Pisa tests is, if you want to have a knowledge economy, an economy based on skills, this is how you measure it.
sentences.zh: 它们正在被这些新兴的、快速发展的国家赶超和超越——你知道的，新加坡、爱沙尼亚、台湾，或者那些我们历史上不认为具有经济竞争力的地区，但我想支持Pisa测试的论点是，如果你想拥有一个知识经济、一个以技能为基础的经济，这就是你衡量它的方式。

sentences.en: We heard that many large European countries are being outpaced by smaller nations.
sentences.zh: 我们听说许多欧洲大国正在被较小的国家赶超。

sentences.en: If someone outpaces you, they are going faster than you – at a higher pace.
sentences.zh: 如果有人 outpace 你，他们就是比你走得更快——以更高的速度。

sentences.en: We use the prefix 'out-' to say that someone or something is better at doing something.
sentences.zh: 我们使用前缀 'out-' 来表示某人或某物在做某事时更胜一筹。

sentences.en: We also heard that smaller nations are 'outperforming' larger ones – they are performing better.
sentences.zh: 我们还听说较小的国家在“outperforming”较大的国家——它们的表现更好。

sentences.en: Singapore, Estonia and Taiwan are described as economic rivals to large European nations – that means that they are competing with them, economically.
sentences.zh: 新加坡、爱沙尼亚和台湾被描述为欧洲大国的经济 rivals（竞争对手）——这意味着它们在经济上与这些大国竞争。

sentences.en: We also heard about a knowledge economy.
sentences.zh: 我们还听到了关于知识经济的说法。

sentences.en: This is an economy based on service industries that require workers to be highly educated, such as IT, finance or advanced engineering.
sentences.zh: 这是一个以服务业为基础的经济，需要受过高等教育的员工，比如IT、金融或高级工程。

sentences.en: So, what makes countries perform better in these tests?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么让国家在这些测试中表现得更好呢？

sentences.en: Let's hear again from BBC World Service programme, 'The Global Story'.
sentences.zh: 让我们再次聆听BBC世界服务部节目《The Global Story》的内容。

sentences.en: Sean Coughlan tells us that those countries that prioritise getting everyone to a certain level do well.
sentences.zh: Sean Coughlan告诉我们，那些优先考虑让每个人达到一定水平的国家做得很好。

sentences.en: We also hear from Rando Kuustik, an Estonian school principal.
sentences.zh: 我们还听取了爱沙尼亚一所学校的校长Rando Kuustik的意见。

sentences.en: Countries which make sure that all their pupils get through a certain level of education to a certain standard, regardless of their background, do well.
sentences.zh: 那些确保所有学生无论其背景如何，都能通过一定水平的教育并达到一定标准国家，表现都很好。

sentences.en: If you are teaching them by different level or abilities, then you are segregating them and we don't want to segregate any people in the world, why we are doing that in the schools?
sentences.zh: 如果你按不同的水平或能力教他们，那么你就是在隔离他们，我们不想在世界上隔离任何人，为什么我们在学校里要这样做呢？

sentences.en: This one of the main things why Estonia is successful.
sentences.zh: 这是爱沙尼亚成功的主要原因之一。

sentences.en: Sean said the most successful systems educate everyone to a particular standard, regardless of their background.
sentences.zh: Sean说，最成功的教育体系让每个人都达到特定的标准，无论其背景如何。

sentences.en: If one thing happens regardless of something else, it means that the something else is not important, or not a problem.
sentences.zh: 如果一件事发生 regardless of 另一件事，这意味着另一件事并不重要，或者不是问题。

sentences.en: Rando Kuustik said that Estonian schools do not want to segregate students.
sentences.zh: Rando Kuustik说，爱沙尼亚的学校不想隔离学生。

sentences.en: Segregate means to separate and keep apart.
sentences.zh: Segregate 的意思是隔离并分开。

sentences.en: So, we've just heard about Estonia, but what about your question, Beth?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们刚刚听说了爱沙尼亚，但是你的问题呢，Beth？

sentences.en: What about those countries? I asked you which out of the USA, Ireland, and the UK came second for reading in the 2022 Pisa rankings.
sentences.zh: 那些国家呢？我问你美国、爱尔兰和英国中，哪个国家在2022年Pisa阅读排名中位列第二。

sentences.en: You said Ireland, and that was the correct answer.
sentences.zh: 你说是爱尔兰，这就是正确的答案。

sentences.en: Well done! OK, let’s recap the vocabulary we’ve learned in this programme about education rankings, starting with contentious - argued about or controversial.
sentences.zh: 干得好！好的，让我们回顾一下本节目中学到的关于教育排名的词汇，首先是 contentious —— 有争议的或引起争论的。

sentences.en: If you're outpaced by someone, they're going faster than you are.
sentences.zh: 如果你被某人 outpaced，说明他们的进展比你快。

sentences.en: Rivals are competitors. A knowledge economy is one based on industries that need highly educated workers, such as IT, finance or advanced engineering.
sentences.zh: Rivals 是竞争对手。知识经济是以需要高学历员工的行业为基础的经济，如IT、金融或高级工程。

sentences.en: If something happens regardless of a second thing, the second thing has no impact on it happening.
sentences.zh: 如果一件事的发生 regardless of 第二件事，说明第二件事对它的发生没有任何影响。

sentences.en: And finally, if people are segregated, different groups of people are separated and kept apart.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果人们被 segregated，不同群体的人就会被分隔开来。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. Remember to visit our website, bbclearningenglish.com, where you’ll find a worksheet and quiz related to this programme, and we’ll see you again soon for more trending topics and useful vocabulary, here at 6 Minute English.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了。记得访问我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，在那里你可以找到与本节目相关的练习题和测验，我们很快就会再见面，带来更多热门话题和实用的词汇，就在6分钟英语。

sentences.en: Goodbye for now! Bye!
sentences.zh: 先说再见啦！拜拜！
